examples.dm: One who does not dwell in form, does not dwell in feeling, One who does not dwell in perception, does not dwell in volition, And one who does not dwell in consciousness, dwells in the nature of reality; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling, Whoever does not abide in perception, does not abide in volition, And whoever does not abide in consciousness, abides in the nature of phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: रुपस्मि यो न स्थिहते न च वेदनायां संज्ञाय यो न स्थिहते न च चेतनायाम् । विज्ञानि यो न स्थिहते स्थितु धर्मतायां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? It is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics; However, because they are completely suffused with wisdom, they are worthy of worship. For example, just as a person who relies on a king receives honor, So too the relics of the Buddha rely upon the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: "If asked why, it is not that I am disrespectful of the bodily relics; But because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped. For example, just as a man relying on a king obtains reverence, The relics of the Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: किं कारणं न मि शरीरि अगौरवत्वं अपि तू खु प्रज्ञपरिभावित पूजयन्ति । यथ राजनिश्रित नरो लभि सर्वि पूजां तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित बुद्धधातुः ॥

examples.dm: Just as a wandering mendicant, through his knowledge of craftsmanship, Brings about the disintegration of the aggregates without any objective apprehension, Any bodhisattva who understands phenomena in that way, Does not touch nirvana, and is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as the wanderer Śreṇika, through his knowledge, Understood the aggregates as unapprehendable and subject to destruction; Whatever bodhisattva understands phenomena in that way Does not contact nirvāṇa, and dwells in wisdom.
examples.sa: अथ श्रेणिकस्य अभुती परिव्राजकस्य ज्ञानोपलम्भु न हि स्कन्धविभावना च । यो बोधिसत्त्व परिजानति एव धर्मां न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: One who rides cannot perceive any direction toward which they go; Though it is said they go to nirvāṇa, no going is perceived. For example, just as when a fire is extinguished there is no going anywhere, For that reason, it is perfectly described as "nirvāṇa."
examples.gm: Whoever mounts it does not apprehend traveling in any direction. Although said to go to nirvana, the going is not apprehended. Just as an extinguished fire has nowhere to go, For this reason it is proclaimed to be "nirvana."
examples.sa: न च लभ्यते य व्रजते दिश आरुहित्वा निर्वाण-ओकगमनं गति नोपलब्धिः । यथ अग्नि निर्वृतु न तस्य गतिप्रचारो सो तेन निर्वृति प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is infinite; It exists above, below, and in all the ten directions as far as they extend. It is without differentiation and without any distinctions.
examples.gm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is boundless; Above, below, and in as many of the ten directions as there are, it exists; There is no difference and there is no distinction.
examples.sa: आकाशधातु पुरिमादिशि दक्षिणायां तथ पश्चिमोत्तरदिशाय अनन्तपारा । उपराधराय दशद्दिशि यावदस्ति नानात्वता न भवते न विशेषप्राप्ता ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: When wise and learned bodhisattvas, contemplating non-arising, Practice in this way, Though they generate great compassion, they have no perception of sentient beings; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whenever a wise, understanding bodhisattva Reflects on non-arising and practices in this way, Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो एवं चरन्तु अनुपादु विचिन्तयित्वा । महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Whether the wise remain in the world or pass into nirvāṇa, This flawless true nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, remains. Bodhisattvas realize this suchness; And therefore, the Buddha is given the name "Tathāgata."
examples.gm: Whether the wise remain in the world or have passed into nirvāṇa, This flawless dharmatā, the emptiness of dharmas, remains; Bodhisattvas subsequently realize this suchness, Therefore, the Buddhas are given the name Tathāgata.
examples.sa: तिष्ठन्तु लोकविदुनां परिनिर्वृतानां स्थित एष धर्मतनियाम शून्यधर्मा । तां बोधिसत्त्व तथताम् अनुबुद्धयन्ति तस्मा हु बुद्ध कृत नाम तथागतेभिः ॥

examples.dm: That which does not exist is called "nonexistent." Foolish beings, having conceptualized it, treat it as either existing or non-existing. Existence and non-existence—these two are phenomena that do not exist. Any bodhisattva who understands this will definitely emerge.
examples.gm: Whatever does not exist is called "non-existent." Fools, examining this, conceive of existence and non-existence. Both existence and non-existence are non-existent phenomena; Whatever bodhisattva knows this will definitely emerge.
examples.sa: योऽसौ न विद्यति स एष अविद्यमानो तां बालु कल्पयि अविद्य करोति विद्याम् । विद्या अविद्य उभि एति असन्त धर्मा निर्याति यो इति प्रजानति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings, completely famished, desire food, And those with minds attached to cyclic existence wander perpetually. The two phenomena of "self" and "mine" are unreal and empty; Yet the foolish, by their own doing, tie knots in the sky.
examples.gm: Fully starving sentient beings desire food, and Those possessing a mind attached to saṃsāra constantly wander. Both self and the phenomena of self are unreal and empty; Childish beings themselves have cast a knot in space.
examples.sa: आहारकाम परिकल्पयमान सत्त्वाः संसारि युक्तमनसः सद संस्मरन्ति । अहु मह्य धर्म उभि एति अभूत शून्या आकाशगण्ठि अयु आत्मन बद्ध बाले ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
examples.gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.
examples.sa: यथ शङ्कितेन विषसंज्ञत अभ्युपैति नो चास्य कोष्ठगतु सो विषु पात्यते च । एमेव बालुपगतो अहु मह्य एषो अहसंज्ञि जायि म्रियते च सदा अभूतो ॥

examples.dm: If one dedicates merit to enlightenment in this way, One is "poison-free," does not forsake the Buddha, and speaks what the Victors have taught. The hero who dedicates in this way outshines All those bodhisattvas in the world who engage in conceptual apprehension.
examples.gm: If one perfectly dedicates merit to awakening in that way, It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and speaks what the Victor has spoken. Dedicating perfectly in that way, the hero outshines all Of however many bodhisattvas there are in the world who possess apprehension.
examples.sa: एवं च पुण्य परिणामयमान बोधौ न च सो हि बुद्ध क्षिपते जिन उक्तवादी । यावन्ति लोकि उपलम्भिकबोधिसत्त्वा अभिभोन्ति सर्वि परिणामयमान शूरो ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, without deep understanding, regards Form, perception, feeling, intention, and consciousness As impermanent, they are practicing a counterfeit; The wise never cause the destruction of phenomena.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva, while lacking full understanding, Fully demonstrates form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness As impermanent, he acts upon fabrication; The wise never destroy dharmas.
examples.sa: सचि रूप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायां चित्तं अनित्य परिणामयि बोधिसत्त्वो । प्र(ति)वर्णिकाय चरते अप्रजानमानो न हि धर्म पण्डित विनाश करोति जातु ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, for many billions of eons, Practices generosity toward Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas and maintains ethical discipline, Cannot match the merit of one who speaks of the Dharma that possesses the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even if that merit from giving and morality were spoken of well.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva, for many thousands of millions of eons, Gives gifts to arhats and pratyekabuddhas and observes ethical discipline, For anyone who teaches the dharma endowed with the supreme perfection of wisdom, Giving and ethical discipline do not bear a fraction of the goodness of that teaching.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व बहुकल्पसहस्रकोटयो दानं ददेयु विमलं तथ शील रक्षे । यश् चैव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रयुक्तो धर्मं भणेय कल पुण्य न दानशीले ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: While practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, They do not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet do not engage in signs; For example, just as a skilled boatman goes back and forth, Without staying on either shore and without remaining in the ocean.
examples.gm: Practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Not touching nirvāṇa and not engaging in signs, Just as a skilled boatman going back and forth, Does not dwell on either shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.
examples.sa: शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं चरमाणु धर्मा न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी । यथ नाविको कुशल गच्छति आरपारम् उभयान्ति अस्थितु न तिष्ठति अर्णवेस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva abides in compassion, Having fully taken up the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom; They contemplate all phenomena as empty, signless, and wishless, And without touching nirvana, they also perceive the true nature of phenomena.
examples.gm: Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in compassion, Completely holding the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom, Realizing that dharmas are empty, signless, and wishless, Does not touch nirvāṇa, yet sees the dharmas.
examples.sa: एमेव स्थित्व करुणां विदु बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाउपायद्वयछत्रपरिगृहीतो । शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं विमृषाति धर्मान् न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति पश्यति धर्मचारी ॥

examples.dm: When, having connected with beings through loving-kindness, He practices the meditative stabilizations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, It is impossible to designate that he has attained nirvana, Or to designate him as something conditioned; he does not abide anywhere.
examples.gm: Whenever, having bound themselves with love for wanderers, They practice the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Can it be designated that they will attain nirvāṇa, Or that they are conditioned? They have no abiding.
examples.sa: यं कालि मैत्रि जगती अनुबन्धयित्वा शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधी चरते समाधिम् । अस्थानमेव यदि निर्वृति प्रापुणेया अथवापि संस्कृत स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः ॥

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: If someone were to take as many sentient beings as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, And, having disciplined them all, establish them in the state of an arhat, Compared to one who writes down this perfection of wisdom, And gives the text to a supreme being, the merit of the latter is far more sublime.
examples.gm: Compared to someone who, in fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tames all however many beings reside there to arhatship, Whoever writes down this perfection of wisdom And gives the book to supreme beings has particularly exalted merit.
examples.sa: यावन्ति गङ्गनदिवालिकतुल्यक्षेत्रे तावन्ति सत्त्व अरहन्ति विनेय कश्चित् । यश् चैव प्रज्ञ इम पारमिता लिखित्वा परसत्त्वि पुस्तकु ददेय विशिष्टपुण्यः ॥

examples.dm: Even if all the sentient beings in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges Were to be considered as having become Māras, And even if each of them emanated that many more from every single hair, All of them together would be unable to create obstacles for the wise.
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in fields equal to the Ganges, If all of them, taking on assumed forms, became Māras, And even if they emanated that many from each and every single hair pore, All of them would not be able to cause hindrances for the wise.
examples.sa: यावन्ति गङ्गनदिवालिसमे हि क्षेत्रे सत्त्वा त सर्वि परिकल्प भवेयु माराः । एकैक रोम पुन तान्तक निर्मिणेय्या सर्वे न शक्य करणे विदु अन्तरायम् ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme Perfection of Wisdom, Do not see any increase or decrease in form. One who does not see phenomena, non-phenomena, or the sphere of phenomena, And does not touch nirvana, is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: When practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, the yogi Does not see the increase or complete decrease of form; Whoever does not see dharma, non-dharma, or the dharmadhātu, And does not touch nirvāṇa, they abide in wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी न च रूपवृद्धि न च पश्यति पारिहाणिम् । धर्मा अधर्म इमु पश्यति धर्मधातुं न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: For example, consider a man who indulges in desire and, Having made an appointment with a woman, fails to meet her; However many conceptual thoughts he experiences in his mind throughout a single day, For that many eons, the bodhisattva will achieve attainment.
examples.gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.
examples.sa: यथ रागधर्मचरितः पुरुषः स्त्रियाये संकेत कृत्व अलभन्तु विवर्तयेया । यावन्ति चित्तचरिता दिवसेन तस्य तावन्त कल्प अनुबुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: Even if they frequent secluded villages, cities, mountain caves, And rely upon remote hermitages and forest retreats, A bodhisattva who praises themselves and disparages others Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
examples.gm: Very solitary villages, cities, and mountain valleys, And isolated monasteries and forests, they thoroughly rely upon; But a bodhisattva who praises themselves and deprecates others, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
examples.sa: प्रविविक्त ग्रामनगरे गिरिकन्दराणि रण्या विविक्त वनप्रस्थ निषेवमाणो । आत्मानुकर्षि पर पंसयि बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्यु मारु पर्युत्थितु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
examples.gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.
examples.sa: ग्रामान्ति यो विहरते अथवा अरण्ये द्वययानचित्तविगतो नियतोऽग्रबोधिम् । एषो विवेकु जगदर्थभिप्रस्थितानां आत्मा क्षिणोति तुलयेय स बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
examples.gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.
examples.sa: परुषं श्रुणित्व वचनं परतो दुरुक्तं परितोषयाति सुसुखं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । को भाषते क शृणुते कुतु कस्य केन सो युक्त क्षान्तिवरपारमिताय विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Whips, sticks, weapons, being killed, bound, or beaten, Decapitation, and the cutting off of ears, feet, hands, and nose— Thinking, "I shall endure whatever worldly sufferings there may be," The bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.gm: "Whips, sticks, weapons, killing, binding, and beating, Severing of the head, and cutting off ears, hands, feet, and nose— Whatever sufferings exist in the world, I will endure them!" Thinking this, the bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.sa: कशदण्डशस्त्रवधबन्धनताडनाश्च शिरछेदकर्णचरणाकरनासछेदाः । यावन्ति दुःख जगती अहु तत्सहामि क्षान्तीय पारमित तिष्ठति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: One who knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in total peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not make illusion one thing and the aggregates another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: मायोपमां य इह जानति पञ्च स्कन्धां न च माय अन्य न च स्कन्ध करोति अन्यान् । नानात्वसंज्ञविगतो उपशान्तचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The bodhisattva does not apprehend a prior limit, a later limit, Or a present; they are the purity of the three times. That which is such is unconditioned and free from conceptual elaboration; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Even if one has honored billions of Buddhas in former lives, If one lacks faith in the Victors' perfection of wisdom, That person of small intelligence, upon hearing it, will reject it; Having rejected it, they become defenseless and go to the Unrelenting Hell.
examples.gm: Even if they honored hundreds of billions of buddhas when practicing previously, If they do not have faith in the perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Upon hearing it, those of small intelligence will abandon it; Having abandoned it, becoming without refuge, they go to the Avīci hell.
examples.sa: सत्कृत्य बुद्धनियुतां परिचारिकायां न च प्रज्ञपारमित श्रद्दधिता जिनानाम् । श्रुत्वा च सो इमु क्षिपिष्यति सोऽल्पबुद्धिः स क्षिपित्व यास्यति अवीचिम् अत्राणभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: Those who, at that time, have become longing and faithful, Having gone to listen to this sublime Dharma, Once they perceive the Dharma preacher to be preoccupied, They will depart without joy and with a troubled mind.
examples.gm: Those who at that time, having become eager and faithful, Go to listen to this holy dharma, Upon knowing that the speaker of dharma is busy with activities, Will depart, devoid of joy and unhappy.
examples.sa: ये चापि तस्मि समये इमु धर्म श्रेष्ठं श्रुणनाय छन्दिक उत्पादयिष्यन्ति श्रद्धाम् । ते धर्मभाणक विदित्वन कार्ययुक्तं प्रेमापनीत गमिष्यन्ति सुदुर्मनाश्च ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the rays of the sun abiding in the sky Dry up the earth and make forms clearly visible, Likewise, the Dharma King, relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and perfectly teaches the Dharma.
examples.gm: For example, just as the rays of the sun dwelling in the sky Dry up this earth and also clearly reveal forms, Likewise, the dharma king, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and also clearly reveals the dharma.
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित यथैव हि सूर्यरश्मि तापेतिमां धरणि दर्शयते च रूपम् । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित धर्मराजो तापेति तृष्णनदि धर्म निदर्शयाति ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: This Dharma of the Leaders is profound and difficult to see; It is not something realized by anyone, nor is it something to be attained. Therefore, the Compassionate Benefactor, having attained awakening, Felt little concern, thinking, "Who among the masses of beings will understand?"
examples.gm: This dharma of the Guides is profound and difficult to see; It is not realized by anyone, nor is it to be attained. Therefore, the Benefactor, the Compassionate One, having discovered enlightenment, Showed little inclination, thinking, "Who among the multitudes of beings will understand?"
examples.sa: गम्भीर धर्म अयु दुर्दृशु नायकानां न च केनचीदधिगतो न च प्रापुणन्ति । एतार्थु बोधिमधिगम्य हितानुकम्पी अल्पोत्सुको क इमु ज्ञास्यति सत्त्वकायो ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: Supreme enlightenment is not reached by the initial mind, Yet without that initial mind, it cannot be reached. Peaceful enlightenment is not attained by the final mind, Yet without that, it is also impossible to attain it.
examples.gm: By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched, Yet without it, one is not able to touch it. By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained, Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.
examples.sa: प्रथमेव चित्त स्पृशती न च अग्रबोधिम् असता न तस्य स्पृशता पुन शक्य भोन्ति । न च चित्त पश्चिम शिवाम् अनुप्रापुणाति असता न तस्य पुन प्रापणनाय शक्यम् ॥

examples.dm: "And such will be the nature of your future ascetic discipline and yoga; Your former qualities were also like this," he declares. Any bodhisattva who, upon hearing such words, becomes conceited, Should be known as one of small intelligence who has been instigated by Māra.
examples.gm: "Whatever ascetic practices, vows, and yogas you will possess, Your past qualities and conduct were also like this," he says. Whatever bodhisattva hears such words and becomes conceited, Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
examples.sa: धुतवृत्त यादृशु स भेष्यति युक्तयोगी पूर्वं पि तुभ्य इमि आसि गुणोवरूपा । यो एव श्रुत्व अभिमन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्यु मारु पर्युत्थितु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: For all the Victors of the past, the future, and those residing in the ten directions, This perfection is the path; there is no other. This perfection is said to be the clarity, the lamp, the light, And the supreme guide for those who have entered upon supreme enlightenment.
examples.gm: The Victorious Ones of the past, future, and whoever abide in the ten directions, The path of all of them is this perfection, and no other. This perfection is, for those entered into supreme awakening, Explained as the supreme illumination, lamp, light, and teacher.
examples.sa: अतिक्रान्तनागत जिना स्थित ये दिशासु सर्वेषु मार्गु अयु पारमिता अनन्यो । ओभास उल्क वरबोधयि प्रस्थितानाम् आलोक शास्त्रि इमि पारमिता प्रदिष्टाः ॥

examples.dm: Just as a person who finds a supreme jewel they had never found before, Is filled with joy at having found it at another time, If they become careless and lose it immediately after finding it, They will suffer constant longing for the jewel they have lost.
examples.gm: A person who previously had not found a supreme jewel, Finding it at another time, out of joy, If they lose it right after finding it by becoming careless, By losing it, desiring the jewel, they will constantly suffer.
examples.sa: पुरुषो य अग्रु रतनस्य अलब्धपूर्वो अपरस्मि कालि पुन लब्ध्व भवेय तुष्टो । स ह लब्ध्व नाशयि पुनोऽपि प्रमादभूतो नाशित्व दुःखि सततं रतनाभिकाङ्क्षी ॥

examples.dm: When training, one does not make any claims about the training; One does not perceive a trainee or the qualities to be trained in, And does not conceptualize between training and non-training— Whoever trains in this way trains here in these Buddha-qualities.
examples.gm: When training, whoever does not assert any training, And does not observe the trainer or the dharmas of training, And does not conceptualize these two: having trained and not having trained, Whoever trains like that, trains in this Dharma of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: यो शिक्षमाणु न उपैति कहिंचि शिक्षां न च शिक्षकं लभति नापि च शिक्षधर्मान् । शिक्षा अशिक्ष उभयो अविकल्पमानो यो शिक्षते स इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: I also rejoice in the mass of merit of all sentient beings, as many as there are, Who strive for virtue and desire to be of benefit; Therefore, once they have attained the qualities of the Victors, They bestow the gift of Dharma upon the world in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: Seeking virtue and desiring to benefit however many sentient beings there are, They also rejoice in the heaps of merit of them all; Therefore, having attained the qualities of the Victorious Ones, In order to exhaust suffering, they give the gift of Dharma to the world.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व कुशलार्थिक मोक्षकामा सर्वेष भोन्ति अनुमोदितु पुण्यराशि । सत्त्वर्थि ते जिनगुण अनन्त प्रापुणित्वा दास्यन्ति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥

examples.dm: To those who practice skillfully in this way, the many hosts of gods Join their palms in reverence and prostrate. All the Buddhas throughout the world systems of the ten directions Likewise utter garlands of praise for their qualities.
examples.gm: To the wise who practice thus, many hosts of gods Join their palms, bow down, and pay homage; And however many Buddhas there are in the world systems of the ten directions, They completely proclaim a garland of praise for their qualities.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु ना पृथुदेवसंघाः कृतअञ्जलीपुट प्रणम्य नमस्ययन्ति । बुद्धा पि यावत दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ गुणवर्णमालपरिकीर्तन कुर्वयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, having attained the fourfold tranquility Of concentration and meditative absorption that bestows joy and bliss, Relinquishes that blissful concentration and the meditative absorptions they have attained, And out of compassion for beings, enters again into the realm of desire.
examples.gm: Similarly, the wise bodhisattva, joy and Having attained the happiness-bestowing four peaceful samādhis of the dhyānas, Lets go of the attainment of the dhyāna samādhis endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, And endowed with compassion for beings, again enters the desire realm.
examples.sa: एमेव ध्यान चतुर् एव समाधि शान्तां लब्ध्वान प्रीति सुखदां विदु बोधिसत्त्वाः । अवसृज्य ध्यानसुखप्रीतिसमाधिलाभं पुन कामधातु प्रविशन्ति जगानुकम्पी ॥

examples.dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: परसत्त्वपुद्गलनिदान विशुद्धसत्त्वा विचरन्ति वीर्यबलपारमिताभियुक्ताः । यथ कुम्भदासि अवशावश भर्तिकस्य तथ सर्वसत्त्ववशतामुपयान्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure, Possessing the thirty-two major marks and infinite power; They proclaim the supreme Dharma of emptiness to sentient beings. Wise and patient, they bring joy to the world.
examples.gm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure; With the thirty-two marks and boundless power and strength, They proclaim the supreme empty dharma to sentient beings; Beings will rejoice in this wise one endowed with patience.
examples.sa: क्षान्तीस्थितस्य परिशुध्यति आत्मभावो द्वात्रिंशलक्षणप्रभाव अनन्तपारो । सत्त्वान शून्यवरधर्म निशामयाती प्रियु भोति सर्वजगती क्षममाणु विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva, thinking, "May this gift be given To all sentient beings throughout the three realms of existence," Bestows the gift, and having done so, Dedicates it to supreme enlightenment for the benefit of all beings.
examples.gm: The wise and brilliant bodhisattva, [thinking], "Of the three states of existence, To all those sentient beings, however many there are, may this gift Be given!" Having thought thus, they give gifts, And also dedicate them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings.
examples.sa: दानं ददित्व विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो यावन्ति सत्त्व त्रिभवे समन्वाहरित्वा । सर्वेषु तेषु भवते अयु दत्तदानं तं चाग्रबोधि परिणामयते जगार्थम् ॥

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, one abandons the various states of animal existence, And by abandoning the eight unfree states, one always finds leisure. Through patience, one will attain a sublime, vast, and beautiful form; With a lovely golden complexion, one becomes worthy of being beheld by all beings.
examples.gm: By discipline, the nature of the manifold destinies of animals and The eight unfree states are abandoned, and leisure is always found. By patience, a fine, supreme, and vast form will be obtained, Golden-colored, beautiful, and worthy to be looked at by beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन तीर्यगति वर्जयि नेकरुपाम् अष्टौ च अक्षण क्षणां लभते स नित्यम् । क्षान्तीय रुप लभते परमं उदारं सुवर्णच्छवि प्रियु जगस्य उदीक्षणीयो ॥

examples.dm: As the supreme physician who heals the ailments of wandering beings, He has spoken this teaching on wisdom, which possesses the path to enlightenment; This path to awakening is titled "The Collection of Precious Qualities," And is taught so that all sentient beings may attain it.
examples.gm: By the supreme physician who heals the diseases of beings, This teaching of wisdom, endowed with the path to awakening, was taught; Its name is the Collection of Precious Qualities, the path to awakening; This path was explained in order for all sentient beings to obtain it.
examples.sa: वैद्योत्तमो जगति रोगचिकित्सकारी प्रज्ञोपदेश कथितो अयु बोधिमार्गो । नामेन रत्नगुणसंचय बोधिमार्गः तं सर्वसत्त्व इतु मार्गतु प्राप्नुवन्ति ॥
